chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a people who make their qufzan smaller, selling by them. He said: 'Those are the ones who undervalue (shortchange) the things of the people.'

key_terms.أَشْيَاءَهُمْ: Their things/property (referring to the customers' goods or money)
key_terms.الْقُفْزَان: A specific type of dry measure or container used for trade
key_terms.يُبْخِسُونَ: They shortchange or undervalue (give less than due)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on using smaller-than-standard measuring devices in trade?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the commercial misconduct of using a smaller-than-standard measuring vessel (qufzan) constitutes *bakhis*, or shortchanging customers. This definition aligns with the Shia scholarly understanding of *ghabn* (deception in trade) and underscores the religious obligation of maintaining precise weights and measures as a fundamental right of the consumer. The ruling highlights that integrity in measurement is not merely a civil contract term but a spiritual duty to ensure fairness in economic transactions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid Al Barqy, from Sa’ad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a people who are making their measuring devices smaller, selling by these. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They are those who are undervaluing the things of the people’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqiy from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
about a people who make al-Qufzan (measuring devices) small with which they sell. He (the Imam) said, ‘They are of the people who cause losses in their belongings.’”
